text:
alex: Heads-up, seeing a spike of ALB target deregistrations in edge-cluster-apac this morning. ~20 targets removed over ~5m. Anyone else?

maya: Yep noticed alerts. ALB console shows 5xx /TARGET_TIMEOUT for health checks. No app crashes in pods. :thinking:

alex: Here's the probe logs from one node:
```bash
# tcpdump from node eth0
13:02:12.123456 IP 34.216.11.22.443 > 10.244.1.7.8080: Flags [S], seq 0
13:02:12.123789 IP 10.244.1.7.8080 > 34.216.11.22.443: Flags [RST]  <-- sometimes no proper reply
```
But we also see kube-proxy/conntrack drops in dmesg: 
```
[ 12345.678901] nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
```

jon: conntrack table full matches. Are these GPU nodes with lots of long-lived connections? I remember autoscaled GPU ASG had a leak last month.

priya: Also check egress policies + SNAT path — if responses are being SNATed or blocked the ALB might treat probes as timed out. What target type is the TG (ip vs instance)?

alex: Target group is "ip" (pods). ALB is probing pod IPs directly. We rolled a calico egress policy last night that denies outbound 0.0.0.0/0 except 443/53 — could be related.

samir: Quick repro: from an affected pod, curl to ALB health endpoint times out. From the node host it succeeds. That suggests reply path from pod -> ALB is being lost or SNATed weirdly.

maya: Temporary workaround: switch TG to "instance" so healthchecks hit NodePort/kube-proxy. We flipped one AZ and deregistrations stopped for that AZ.

alex: Applied instance-target fallback for ai-hostpool-apac in that AZ. Deregs stopped after ~2m. Monitoring now.

jon: My hypothesis: conntrack exhaustion + restrictive egress policy. ALB probes spawn lots of tiny conntrack entries. If nodes already have many long-lived entries (model serving TCPs), conntrack table becomes full and kernel drops new packets -> ALB sees timeout -> deregister.

priya: Longterm fixes to consider:
- raise net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max on GPU node AMI and ensure it persists
- update calico egress to explicitly allow ALB health CIDR ranges (or health-port)
- keep instance-target TG as an emergency fallback OR consider hostNetwork for health endpoints
- add alert for nf_conntrack table full / drop counters per node

samir: Also plan a kube-proxy/kernel patch — older kube-proxy had incomplete conntrack cleanup when services change which exacerbates table saturation.

alex: Action items (creating tickets):
- INFRA-3245: bump nf_conntrack_max on GPU AMI + bake new image
- INFRA-3246: add ALB health CIDR allow rule to calico egress in edge clusters
- INFRA-3247: runbook for emergency failover to instance target groups
- INFRA-3248: alerting for conntrack drops and high conntrack utilization

infra-bot: alert: suppressed 23 target_deregister events in ap-southeast-1 -> incident created and summary posted to #incidents

maya: I'll push hotfix today to increase conntrack sysctl on the GPU ASG nodes and coordinate AMI bake with ops.

alex: Note cost/ops tradeoff: instance targets add per-node CPU overhead handling more traffic, so keep as rollback-only fallback.

jon: After the sysctl bump and AMI rollout on a small canary, conntrack usage dropped and ALB stayed stable. I'll export prometheus graphs to the ticket.

priya: Also let's increase readinessProbe initialDelay for models that do heavy GPU init — often containers take >15s to warm which causes transient fail counts during scaleups.

samir: Marking this resolved for now: instance-target fallback + conntrack bump applied. Follow-ups scheduled in INFRA board.

alex: Thanks everyone. Please attach any follow-up logs to the tickets and ping if we see a recurrence. :thumbsup:
